title: Embeddings: Queue Smoothing, Warm Pools, and Rate-shaping for Stable Throughput
creator: Maya Singh
description: Problem: Our embeddings endpoint shows high variance in per-request latency and bursty GPU utilization under mixed tenant workloads. This causes slow tail latencies for small single-item embedding calls and inefficient GPU packing during steady-state. Goal: reduce p95 embedding latency variance, increase steady-state throughput utilization, and improve autoscaler responsiveness while keeping unit cost stable. Scope: queueing algorithm, ingress shaping (per-tenant token-bucket), warm worker pools (keep a small number of containers/VMs pre-warmed to avoid cold-starts for single-item requests), batch sizing heuristics (min/max batch sizes and adaptive packing), and autoscaler tuning (scale-up/down latency thresholds + rate/burst protection). Out of scope for this ticket: model architecture changes and storage-level sharding of embedding indexes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end load test (mixed 60/30/10 small/medium/large requests) shows p95 latency <= 300ms for single-item embeddings and p50 <= 120ms
GPU utilization increases by >= 12% for steady-state 5k rps workload without increasing cost per 1M embeddings by > 5%
Autoscaler reacts to a 3x ingress spike within 90 seconds (scale-up) and scales down to baseline within 8 minutes without oscillation
No regressions in embedding vector correctness; regression tests pass for canonical prompt set
Feature rollout toggle available in console per-tenant and observable metrics added to Dashboards (ingress queue length, warm-pool size, smoothed ingress rate)
metrics: effective throughput (embeddings/sec) and cost per 1M embeddings
autoscale reaction time (sec) and number of scaling steps
queue length and average wait time (ms)
runbook_notes: If queue length > 1000 for >5 minutes, enable emergency rate-shaping mode (global throttle) and notify on-call. Warm-pool min size can be increased in console temporarily. For suspected kernel regressions, revert runtime-1.22 warm-pool patches and re-run smoke tests.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal A/B: roll to 10% of traffic (non-critical tenants) for 48h, monitor latency/throughput/cost; 2) Gradually expand to 50% over 72h with automated rollback if p95 increases by > 10%; 3) Full rollout and deprecation of old queue algorithm after two successful weeks and sign-off from SRE and ML QA.
risks: Incorrect batch sizing could increase latency for small requests if min-batch timeouts are too long. Warm pools increase idle GPU hours (cost). Per-tenant shaping needs correct burst budget calculation to avoid unfair throttling. Autoscaler hysteresis tuning may need multiple iterations to avoid thrash.
test_plan: Synthetic mixed-workload harness in k6 + local GPU cluster: 3 phases (steady, burst, back-to-steady). Record latencies, utilization, and scaling events. Run regression embedding similarity tests. Add post-deploy Canary dashboard and automated alerts for p95 and failed embeddings.
next_steps: 1) Merge design PR and infra changes for warm-pool metadata; 2) Implement ingress token-bucket and leaky-bucket queue smoothing; 3) Add adaptive batcher with time-based flush and max-wait safeguards; 4) Run 3 k6 load tests and iterate thresholds; 5) Schedule canary rollout and monitor; 6) Postmortem/lessons-learned after rollout.
